page: Hetzner Cloud cpx62 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 16 vCPUs and 16 physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, utilizing the QEMU hypervisor. The system is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 640 GB NVMe SSD, while no dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance in specific memory and decompression tasks. The server achieves top-tier results in large-block memory bandwidth, with read-only speeds of 277.56 GB/sec and write speeds of 137.51 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and single-core stress-ng CPU performance also rank in the top 25 percent of tested systems. However, multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and database operations fall within the average range. Large-model LLM inference is constrained by the hardware profile, though smaller 135M model inference shows strong token generation speeds.

From a resource density perspective, the cpx62 offers a high-capacity NVMe storage allocation relative to its shared CPU architecture, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring substantial local disk space without dedicated CPU cores. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-core loads, as reflected in its average multi-core benchmark scores.

This server is suited for multi-threaded decompression tasks, light LLM inference with smaller models, software compilation, and static web serving. It also functions well for general-purpose workloads that benefit from fast NVMe storage and high memory bandwidth but do not require dedicated, non-shared CPU resources.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx62 is an x86_64 virtual server featuring 16 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 31.0 GB of RAM and a 640 GB NVMe SSD. Operating under the QEMU hypervisor, this configuration delivers strong single-core CPU performance and high uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 277.56 GB/sec for large-block reads. While multi-core CPU and database benchmarks sit in the average tier due to the shared CPU allocation, the server excels in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and small-model LLM inference. The cpx62 offers a cost-efficient balance of high-capacity local storage and memory bandwidth, making it highly suitable for software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight data processing tasks that do not demand dedicated CPU resources.
